description: Written exam starter bank for the monthly exams. 30 questions support 12 deterministic 10-question sets.
ruleset: GBA-era 2006 rules; 8000 LP; 40-60 Main Deck; 20 Fusion Deck
source: 2006-era Yu-Gi-Oh! rules and the GBA manual; GBA-specific answers marked medium until A01 verifies.

questions.text: How many Normal Summons (including Tribute Summons) may a player perform per turn?
questions.explanation: A player may Normal Summon or Set exactly one monster per turn. Tribute Summoning is a Normal Summon.

questions.text: How many Tributes are required to Normal Summon a Level 7 monster?
questions.explanation: Level 7-8 monsters require two Tributes.

questions.text: How many Tributes are required to Normal Summon a Level 5 monster?
questions.explanation: Level 5-6 monsters require one Tribute.

questions.text: How many Life Points does each player start with in a standard duel?
questions.explanation: Duel Academy uses the standard 8000 LP starting total.

questions.text: What is the legal size of a Main Deck in this game?
questions.explanation: The Main Deck must contain 40 to 60 cards.

questions.text: What is the maximum size of the Fusion/Extra Deck in the GBA game?
questions.explanation: Duel Academy allows up to 20 Fusion Deck cards.
questions.source: GBA rule; TCG of the era used 15

questions.text: How many copies of the same card may a deck contain (ignoring the banned/limited list)?
questions.explanation: The standard limit is three copies of a card by name.

questions.text: How many Monster Card Zones does each player have?
questions.explanation: Each player has five Monster Card Zones.

questions.text: How many Spell & Trap Card Zones does each player have?
questions.explanation: Each player has five Spell & Trap Card Zones, plus a Field Zone.

questions.text: What is the hand limit during the End Phase?
questions.explanation: A player must discard down to six cards in the End Phase.

questions.text: When may a monster attack directly?
options: Only if the opponent controls no monsters
questions.explanation: A direct attack is allowed when the opponent controls no monsters (unless a card says otherwise).

questions.text: A monster attacks an opponent's Defense Position monster with higher DEF. What happens?
options: The attacking player takes the difference as battle damage
The defending player takes the difference
questions.explanation: If ATK is lower than DEF, the attacking player takes the difference as battle damage. The defending player takes no damage from a normal attack on a Defense Position monster.

questions.text: When an attack targets a face-down Defense Position monster, when is it flipped face-up?
questions.explanation: The monster is flipped face-up during damage calculation, before damage is applied.

questions.text: What card is normally required to Fusion Summon a Fusion Monster?
questions.explanation: Polymerization (or a card that names itself as a Fusion substitute) performs a standard Fusion Summon.

questions.text: What is required to Ritual Summon a Ritual Monster?
options: A Ritual Spell Card and the required Tributes
questions.explanation: Ritual Summoning requires the matching Ritual Spell Card and Tributes whose total Level meets the requirement.

questions.text: What happens when a player cannot draw a card because their Deck is empty?
options: They shuffle their Graveyard into the Deck
questions.explanation: A player who cannot draw loses by deck-out.

questions.text: What happens when a player's Life Points reach zero?
options: The duel continues for one more turn
questions.explanation: Reaching 0 LP loses the duel immediately.

questions.text: Which phase follows Main Phase 1?
questions.explanation: The normal order is Draw, Standby, Main 1, Battle, Main 2, End.

questions.text: When does Main Phase 2 occur?
questions.explanation: Main Phase 2 is entered after the Battle Phase, before the End Phase.

questions.text: When a chain resolves, which effect resolves first?
options: The effect with the highest Spell Speed
questions.explanation: Chains resolve last-in, first-out: the last effect activated resolves first.

questions.text: Which card type has Spell Speed 2?
questions.explanation: Quick-Play Spell Cards are Spell Speed 2. Normal Traps are also Spell Speed 2.

questions.text: What Spell Speed are Counter Trap Cards?
questions.explanation: Counter Traps are Spell Speed 3 and can respond to Spell Speed 2 effects.

questions.text: When can a Trap Card normally be activated after it is Set?
questions.explanation: A Trap must normally remain Set for one turn before it can be activated.

questions.text: Where is a Field Spell Card placed?
questions.explanation: Field Spell Cards are placed in the Field Zone.

questions.text: Which statement about a Normal Monster is correct?
questions.explanation: Normal Monsters have no card effects.

questions.text: Which statement about an Effect Monster is correct?
options: It has an effect that can change the game state
questions.explanation: Effect Monsters have at least one card effect.

questions.text: How do you win with Exodia the Forbidden One?
options: Have all five Forbidden One pieces in hand
questions.explanation: Having all five Exodia pieces in hand wins the duel immediately.

questions.text: When you Set a monster, what position is it in?
questions.explanation: A Set monster is placed face-down in Defense Position.

questions.text: What does a Flip Summon do?
options: Changes a face-down Defense monster to face-up Attack
Changes a face-up Attack monster to Defense
Returns a monster to the hand
questions.explanation: A Flip Summon flips a face-down Defense Position monster into face-up Attack Position.

questions.text: Is a Tribute Summon a type of Normal Summon?
options: No, it is a Special Summon
questions.explanation: Tribute Summoning is a Normal Summon that uses Tributes, and it uses the once-per-turn Normal Summon.
